item.title: Lagos shuts Ejigbo Fire Station after alleged assault
item.description: By Evelyn Usman The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service has indefinitely closed its Ejigbo Fire Station following reported repeated assaults on its personnel, calling for an impartial investigation into the incidents. The Service said the decision was taken to protect firefighters and firefighting equipment after personnel were allegedly attacked at the station on Tuesday, October 13, and again on Friday, October 16, 2026. According to the Service, the first incident was reported to the Ejigbo Police Station. However, the alleged assailants reportedly returned days later and disrupted operations despite the intervention of senior police authorities. The Controller-General of the Service, Mrs Margaret Adeseye, condemned the reported attacks, warning that violence against emergency responders could undermine public safety and effective emergency service delivery. In a statement, Adeseye said the incidents had raised serious concerns about the safety of firefighters and other emergency responders responsible for protecting lives and property across Lagos State. She stressed that personnel must be able to perform their statutory duties without fear of violence, intimidation or unlawful interference. “Attacks on emergency responders can compromise operational readiness, delay emergency interventions and expose members of the public to avoidable risks,” she said. Adeseye said the Ejigbo station would remain closed indefinitely pending a satisfactory resolution of the matter. She added that personnel and firefighting equipment attached to the station would be temporarily redeployed to an undisclosed location for security reasons. According to her, the measure is intended to safeguard personnel and equipment while ensuring continuity of emergency response operations in the affected area. The Controller-General urged relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough, impartial and professional investigation to establish the facts and take appropriate action, in accordance with the law, against anyone found responsible. Reaffirming the Service’s commitment to protecting lives and property across Lagos State, Adeseye said it would continue to work with relevant authorities to address the security concerns and ensure that firefighters could operate in a safe environment. item.title: Kalu mourns former Delta Governor, Uduaghan
item.description: Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan. Kalu described Uduaghan’s death as a painful loss to his family, the people of Delta State and Nigeria at large. In a statement on Monday, the senator said the late governor would be remembered for his contributions to governance, healthcare and infrastructure development in Delta State. “I received with great sadness the news of the passing of former Governor of Delta State, His Excellency, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan. “His death is a painful loss to his family, the people of Delta State and Nigeria at large,” Kalu said. He described Uduaghan as an accomplished medical doctor, experienced administrator and dedicated public servant who devoted many years to serving the people of Delta State. Kalu noted that Uduaghan held several key positions in the state before becoming governor in 2007. “Dr Uduaghan was an accomplished medical doctor, experienced administrator and dedicated public servant who contributed immensely to the development of Delta State. “From his years as Commissioner for Health and Secretary to the State Government to his tenure as governor, he demonstrated a commitment to public service and the welfare of his people,” he said. Kalu said Uduaghan’s contributions to public service, particularly in healthcare, governance and infrastructure development, would remain part of his legacy. “His contributions to governance, healthcare and infrastructural development will remain part of his legacy,” he added. The Abia North senator extended his condolences to Uduaghan’s wife, children and the entire family, as well as the government and people of Delta State and the late governor’s former colleagues and associates. “At this difficult moment, I extend my heartfelt sympathies to his wife, children, the entire Uduaghan family, the government and people of Delta State, and all those who knew and worked with him. “May Almighty God grant his soul eternal rest and give his family the strength to bear this painful loss,” Kalu said. item.title: 2027: City Boy Movement targets Oyo grassroots for Tinubu
item.description: By Adeola Badru The City Boy Movement (CBM) in Oyo State has begun strengthening its grassroots structures across the state’s 33 local government areas to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. The movement unveiled its strategy on Monday in Ibadan during the inauguration of its state and local government executive councils, where leaders urged members to prioritise collective interests, strengthen grassroots networks and work towards electoral victories for the APC at all levels. Speaking on behalf of the State Director, Femi Onireti, Olumide Alli urged members to set aside personal interests and commit themselves to advancing the movement’s collective political objectives. He said the movement was established to secure Tinubu’s re-election and support other APC candidates in the 2027 polls, stressing the need to translate its numerical strength into effective grassroots mobilisation. Alli said the Tinubu administration deserved another term, citing its performance across various sectors of the economy and the continuation of projects inherited from previous administrations. “Tinubu in the past three years has touched all the sectors of the economy. item.title: Tinubu: Uduaghan devoted leadership to Delta’s development
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has mourned former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, describing him as a public servant whose leadership was devoted to the state’s development and service to Nigeria. Tinubu, in a condolence message, extended his sympathies to the Uduaghan family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state over the death of the former governor at the age of 71. The message read: “It is with a heavy heart that I extend my condolences to the Uduaghan family, the government, and the people of Delta State on the passing of former Governor Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, at 71. “Dr Uduaghan was a public servant whose leadership was devoted to Delta State’s development and service to our nation. “He served as Commissioner for Health, Secretary to the State Government and was elected Governor of Delta State in 2007. His two-term tenure, which ended in 2015, placed him at the centre of the state’s political and developmental journey. “During this period, he pursued developmental strides to improve infrastructure, healthcare delivery, and the overall welfare of Deltans.” The President said Uduaghan remained active in Delta State’s political and socio-economic landscape after leaving office, contributing to democratic governance and public service. He described the former governor’s death as a great loss to his family, community, Delta State and the country. Tinubu urged the people of Delta State to draw strength from Uduaghan’s years of service and the enduring relationships he built across the country’s political and social spheres. “On behalf of my family, the Government, and the people of Nigeria, I extend my deepest sympathies to his wife, Roli; his children; his cousin, former Governor James Ibori; and friends and political associates whose lives he impacted. “May Almighty God grant his soul eternal rest and comfort all who mourn him,” the President said. item.title: Governors mourn Uduaghan, honour his public service
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF), comprising the 36 state governors, has mourned former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, who died at the age of 71, days before his 72nd birthday. The governors said Uduaghan’s tenure from 2007 to 2015 formed a significant chapter in Delta State’s governance history and contributed to efforts to address the needs and aspirations of its people. In a condolence statement issued on Monday and signed by the NGF Director of Media and Strategic Communications, Yunusa Tanko Abdullahi, the forum’s chairman, Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara State, expressed deep sorrow over Uduaghan’s death. The statement read, “The Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF), H.E. AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, has expressed deep sorrow over the passing of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, who reportedly died at the age of 71 following a brief illness. “Dr Uduaghan served as Governor of Delta State from 2007 to 2015, a period during which he was involved in advancing the state’s development priorities and public administration. His years in office formed a significant chapter in Delta State’s governance history and contributed to the ongoing efforts to address the needs and aspirations of its people.” The forum acknowledged Uduaghan’s years of public service and the responsibilities he undertook in leading Delta State, describing his death as a moment of grief for his family, associates and the wider community. It extended condolences to his family and loved ones, as well as others mourning his passing, and expressed solidarity with the people of Delta State during the period of mourning. “The Forum honours his memory and recognises his place in the history of governance in Delta State. We wish all who are grieving the strength and fortitude to navigate this period of mourning,” the statement added. item.title: Fuel subsidy return could push Naira to ₦4,000/$ — Oyedele
item.description: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has warned that a return to petrol subsidy could trigger capital flight, weaken investor confidence and push the naira to between ₦3,000 and ₦4,000 to the dollar. Oyedele gave the warning on Monday during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. He said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle. The minister ruled out reversing the reforms, warning that even a signal that President Bola Tinubu’s administration was considering reinstating petrol subsidy could unsettle financial markets, increase borrowing costs and worsen economic pressures on households. “In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious,” he said. Oyedele warned that any indication of a possible return to subsidy would trigger an immediate market reaction. “If, for any reason, the President were to say we are merely considering the return of fuel subsidy, capital would react immediately. “Airfares would struggle, the naira would come under severe pressure, potentially moving towards 3,000, 3,500 or even 4,000. The very fuel people want subsidised would become far more expensive in naira terms,” he said. The minister said capital flight could extend beyond foreign investors, as wealthy Nigerians, business owners and middle-class investors might also turn to the dollar as a hedge against uncertainty, further increasing demand for foreign exchange. He warned that ordinary Nigerians would ultimately bear the consequences through higher import costs, rising prices and increased economic hardship. Oyedele also rejected suggestions that the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s temporary reduction in petrol retail margins amounted to a return to subsidy. He explained that the reduction was a commercial decision rather than a payment funded by public resources, arguing that a company’s decision to lower its profit margin to make a product more affordable should not automatically be classified as a subsidy. President Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, during his inauguration at Eagle Square, Abuja. “Subsidy is gone,” Tinubu declared shortly after being sworn in as Nigeria’s 16th president. He said the national budget would make no provision for petrol subsidy from June 2023, marking a major shift in the country’s fuel pricing policy. item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to stop giving money to people in Nigeria who ask them for financial help, saying continued assistance may ease the effects of hardship without addressing its underlying causes. Obi attributed Nigeria’s economic hardship to poor leadership and argued that financial assistance does not address that problem, urging Nigerians in the diaspora to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for productive leaders. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” Obi said at a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. He argued that people’s continued need for financial help was connected to the country’s economic difficulties, which he blamed on poor governance. In his view, sending money can cushion the hardship people face, but it does not resolve the problems that have left them seeking assistance. The former Anambra State governor also pointed to his record in public office, saying he had saved public funds during his tenure. He acknowledged that he was not perfect, but argued that his record set him apart from other governors. “I’m not saying I’m a saint, but I saved money. I’ve not seen one governor who has saved 10 per cent of what I saved. No governor has done it,” Obi said. He further challenged other governors to match the savings he said he achieved while in office, saying: “I was not the only governor, and I challenge people if one governor can save 10 per cent of the money I saved, but there is nobody that did that.” The NDC presidential candidate further implored Nigerians to begin by supporting leaders they consider less corrupt. “Let’s start with this one that is less corrupt. That’s how other countries change,” he added. He also said his conversations with people reinforced the need for collective responsibility, adding that building a new Nigeria would require citizens to take an active role in addressing the country’s challenges. Obi urged Nigerians to take the 2027 election seriously, describing it as a critical moment for the country. item.title: NAF lowers water level at Igbokoda crash site
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has reported significant progress in dewatering operations at the site of the crashed ATR 42-500 aircraft, NAF 931, in Igbokoda, Ondo State, as recovery efforts entered their 14th day on Monday. The Air Force said continuous pumping had substantially reduced the water level at the crash site, with the recovery team working to remove most of the remaining water, subject to prevailing conditions. In a statement issued on Monday, the Director of Public Relations and Information, Headquarters, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said efforts were also ongoing to reinforce the embankment with sandbags to prevent collapse and maintain stability during the dewatering process. According to the Service, the operation requires sustained engineering and water-removal efforts under challenging conditions, reflecting the scale and complexity of the recovery mission. The NAF commended the dedication and professionalism of recovery personnel and partner agencies, particularly Hitech Construction Company, for supporting the ongoing operation. The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, also praised the recovery team for its resilience and professionalism, reaffirming the Service’s commitment to completing the operation safely and methodically. The Air Force added that recovery efforts were continuing alongside the ongoing investigation into the aircraft accident. Expressing sympathy with the bereaved families, the Service acknowledged the pain and anguish caused by the tragedy and reiterated its commitment to sustaining recovery operations and providing timely, verified updates. It also appreciated the patience and cooperation of the Igbokoda community and the continued support of other stakeholders as the operation progresses. item.title: Witchcraft Accusation: Bauchi police arrest 17 suspects
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested 17 suspects over an alleged witchcraft accusation that triggered a violent attack on a 60-year-old man and his family in Gobirawa Village, Alkaleri Local Government Area. The suspects allegedly attacked the man and his 30-year-old son after accusing the son of witchcraft following the death of a 20-year-old resident, Halilu Ahmad, on October 16, 2026. The attack reportedly occurred around 1am on October 18, when the suspects allegedly invaded the family’s residence armed with machetes and sticks, inflicting multiple injuries on the victims. The attackers also allegedly damaged two motorcycles belonging to the family. The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the attack was triggered by the suspects’ belief that the victim’s son was responsible for the death through witchcraft. The 60-year-old victim was initially taken to General Hospital, Alkaleri, for treatment but was later referred to Ihsan Hospital, Bauchi, due to the severity of his condition. Police spokesman, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed the arrests in a statement on Monday, saying detectives attached to the Alkaleri Division apprehended the 17 suspects following the incident. He said the Commissioner of Police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, had directed the transfer of the case to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Bauchi, for discreet investigation. According to Habib, the commissioner also ordered efforts to apprehend three other suspects still at large. Aliyu warned residents against witchcraft accusations and unverified superstitious beliefs that could trigger violence and the unlawful punishment of innocent people. He urged residents to report suspicions, grievances and criminal allegations to the police rather than resorting to self-help or jungle justice. The commissioner assured the public that the command would pursue justice in the case and would not tolerate actions capable of threatening public peace and security. People in private groups or community circles often get wind of winning numbers from messages that seem to appear out of nowhere. These updates move so quickly that official channels can feel a step behind, raising questions about what information people trust and how quickly it shapes opinions. Close-knit WhatsApp groups push numbers first This quick movement of information is fueled by the way WhatsApp groups function—close, trusted circles where news spreads almost instantly among friends and acquaintances. When someone hears a rumor or gets an early heads-up about the latest lottery numbers, they’ll often share it with their group before checking if it’s official. The excitement of being first can feel more important than waiting for confirmation. item.title: UEFA gives Infantino deadline to release key FIFA documents
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye UEFA has given FIFA president Gianni Infantino until 2 November to release key documents on the organisation’s governance and decision-making, warning that several fundamental questions remain unanswered. According to the BBC, UEFA general secretary Theodore Theodoridis set out the deadline in a letter to FIFA. The letter said the global governing body had not addressed “a number of fundamental questions”. “Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon,” the letter added. The request follows Thursday’s FIFA Council meeting, where president Gianni Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan but did not release documents related to the proposal. UEFA also sent FIFA an eight-page document outlining concerns about several matters, including the FIFA Forward Enterprise private investment proposal, the FIFA Peace Prize and the suspended ban involving United States forward Folarin Balogun. FIFA has been approached for comment. Infantino has led FIFA since 2016 and is seeking a third term as president. item.title: Court ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​⁠⁠​​​​‍‌​dismisses Sowore’s request seeking DSS DG to testify in his defence
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday dismissed an application by Omoyele Sowore, publisher of Sahara Reporters, seeking an order compelling the Director-General (DG) of Department of State Services (DSS), Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi, to testify in his defence. Justice Mohammed Umar, in a ruling, held that the application by Sowore, the presidential candidate of Action Action Congress (AAC), would not serve the interest of justice. Justice Umar held that the DG or any designated officer of the service who had full knowledge of its official and other relevant business could testify before this court for the defendant (Sowore). The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Sowore is being prosecuted by the DSS on allegations bordering on cybercrime. The defendant was alleged to have, in August 2025, published posts on X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook, describing President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accusing him of lying about the level of corruption in the country. Sowore, through his lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide Fusika, SAN, had sought an order of the court compelling the DG’s appearance to testify relating to the cyberbullying case instituted against him. The DSS’ lawyer, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, had opposed the move, arguing that another official of the agency could testify on his behalf. The senior lawyer argued that it was absurd for Sowore to insist on the DSS DG’s appearance in court in an action that was purely official and not personal. In his ruling, Justice Umar agreed with Kehinde’s argument that the subpoena concerned an official act of the DSS and that the expected testimony was not personal to the DG. According to the judge the testimony that is expected from the Director General is not personal, but in respect of an official act or engagement. Justice Umar consequently ruled that another DSS official could appear to give evidence on the agency’s behalf. Following the ruling, defence counsel called the 3rd defence witness, Michael Jego, an investigating officer with the DSS. Jego said he was a member of the DSS investigation team which flagged the controversial post of Sowore on X and Facebook and subsequently advised him to retract it. ‎ ‎The witness said the posts made on 26 Aug. 2025 had the potential of posing a significant threat to national security. The witness told the court that he was part of an investigation team that monitored reactions with relation to the post. item.title: Japan to launch world-first mission to moon of Mars
item.description: Japanese scientists will launch a spacecraft on Tuesday that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars’s moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth. The flagship H3 rocket carrying the unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe is set to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 am (1941 GMT Monday), according to the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). If successful, the spacecraft will arrive near Mars around August next year, where it will orbit one of its moons, Phobos. It will later land on Phobos and collect at least 10 grams (0.35 ounces) of material from the surface during its planned three years in the Red Planet’s vicinity. The mission — which aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region — is a collaboration with US and European space agencies, as well as numerous universities and tech companies. Those involved hope that it will help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration. JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born. One theory for the origin of the moons — the “giant impact” hypothesis — is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars. The “capture” hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids pulled in by Mars’s gravity. Determining which theory is correct will help reveal “how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets”, JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun — Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. – ‘Natural space station’ – JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a “natural space station” by establishing the requirements for a round trip — something “essential for crewed Mars exploration”. It will also observe the planet’s other moon, Deimos, although it will not land on it. US and Chinese space agencies have also been vying to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth. NASA’s Perseverance rover, which has been roaming across Mars since 2021, has already collected samples. The return mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by Congress in January. China’s Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 — potentially before the Japanese mission’s return. item.title: CAN mourns Uduaghan, hails commitment to national unity
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has mourned former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, praising his commitment to dialogue and confidence-building during a period of heightened political tension in Nigeria. The association said Uduaghan’s efforts to promote understanding and preserve national unity remained an important part of his contributions to public service and nation-building. In a statement on Monday, CAN President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, expressed sadness over the former governor’s death and extended the association’s sympathies to his family, the Delta State Government and the people of Delta State, as well as all those mourning him. “His commitment to dialogue, confidence-building and the preservation of national unity remains worthy of commendation,” Archbishop Okoh said. He described Uduaghan’s passing as a loss to his family and all who valued his contributions to public service and nation-building. Archbishop Okoh prayed for God’s comfort for the bereaved family and others affected by the loss, asking God to grant the former governor eternal rest. item.title: FG Reaffirms Commitment To Human Capital Development For Economic Growth
item.description: The Federal Government has reaffirmed its commitment to human capital development as a central pillar for economic growth, saying long-term investments in health, education, skills and livelihoods are critical to transforming Nigeria’s economy. The reaffirmation was made during a media engagement in Abuja on Monday organised to keep journalists abreast of developments under the Human Capital Development Programme (HCD) 2.0 and deepen public understanding of its role in national development. National Coordinator of the Human Capital Development 2.0 Programme, Rukayya El-Rufai, said Nigeria’s economic future depends on deliberate and sustained investment in its people. “Nigeria’s future depends on its people. If we do not invest in them, we cannot grow our economy. There’s a lot of investment going into infrastructure, but if you do not invest in human capital, you are not simply going to be able to grow your economy as much,” he said. El-Rufai explained that HCD 2.0 builds on the earlier version introduced under former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, which focused on health, education and labour force participation. According to her, the new iteration expands the scope to include skills development and livelihoods, to address poverty, underemployment and learning poverty. She said the programme is evidence-led and tracks under-five mortality, immunisation coverage, stunting, out-of-school rates, learning poverty and youth employment as six priority indicators. “The one that worries me and scares me is that learning poverty is so high – about 70 percent,” she said. “When kids are in school, what they’re learning is not sufficient.” According to her, the programme is embedded within the National Economic Council to ensure integration with productivity and resource allocation decisions. El-Rufai noted that while the framework is national, states are expected to adapt it to their peculiar developmental challenges, stressing that there is no one-size-fits-all approach. “Each state is now developing its own HCD plan, guided by its unique challenges,” she said. item.content:encoded: The Federal Government has reaffirmed its commitment to human capital development as a central pillar for economic growth, saying long-term investments in health, education, skills and livelihoods are critical to transforming Nigeria’s economy. The reaffirmation was made during a media engagement in Abuja on Monday organised to keep journalists abreast of developments under the Human Capital Development Programme (HCD) 2.0 and deepen public understanding of its role in national development. National Coordinator of the Human Capital Development 2.0 Programme, Rukayya El-Rufai, said Nigeria’s economic future depends on deliberate and sustained investment in its people. “Nigeria’s future depends on its people. If we do not invest in them, we cannot grow our economy. There’s a lot of investment going into infrastructure, but if you do not invest in human capital, you are not simply going to be able to grow your economy as much,” he said. El-Rufai explained that HCD 2.0 builds on the earlier version introduced under former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, which focused on health, education and labour force participation. According to her, the new iteration expands the scope to include skills development and livelihoods, to address poverty, underemployment and learning poverty. She said the programme is evidence-led and tracks under-five mortality, immunisation coverage, stunting, out-of-school rates, learning poverty and youth employment as six priority indicators. “The one that worries me and scares me is that learning poverty is so high – about 70 percent,” she said. “When kids are in school, what they’re learning is not sufficient.” According to her, the programme is embedded within the National Economic Council to ensure integration with productivity and resource allocation decisions. El-Rufai noted that while the framework is national, states are expected to adapt it to their peculiar developmental challenges, stressing that there is no one-size-fits-all approach. “Each state is now developing its own HCD plan, guided by its unique challenges,” she said. She cited ongoing state-level innovations, including Imo State’s “One Child, One Business” initiative, Nasarawa State’s gender mainstreaming in its HCD plan, and Anambra State’s digital skills training and startup grants for youths. On sustainability, she said the Federal Government is advocating for political parties to sign a compact that treats human capital investment as a sovereign imperative that transcends administrations. Project Manager for the HCD Programme, Doossur Zasha, urged the media to sustain public conversation around human capital development and translate policy concepts into everyday realities. “The media can take conversations from abstract language to things people can relate to daily.
